title: CircleCI: Dynamic config setup
body: ## What I did Related: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/19476 Tracking: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/32936 I'm overhauling the CI config. In this PR I introduce the `scripts/ci` folder, in which a CircleCI config is dynamically generated. This dynamic generation allows us to check the repo/PR/branch state and read dynamic config files (such as `sandboxes-templates.ts`) to determine what the optimum CI workflow would look like. Here's is an overview: The hope is that in the future, we'll be able to do change detection, and instead of adding `ci:*`-labels to PRs, we automatically only run affected sandboxes. ### Testing #### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests: - [x] stories - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] end-to-end tests #### Manual testing - [x] We should run this PR with each `ci:*`-label at least once, checking if every runs as expected. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Replaced many legacy CI workflows with a dynamic CI config generator and centralized CI tooling; removed numerous static CI jobs and an unstable sandbox template. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved CLI logging resilience and added an environment guard to optionally skip Playwright installation. * **Documentation** * Expanded CONTRIBUTING with local development and sandbox-filtering guidance. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

My latest knowledge is that `inDevelopment` sandboxes are now also running on CI.

What is the workflow to add a new sandbox and could you maybe document it somewhere (if not already documented)?

Something like:
1. Add a new sandbox in `sandbox-templates`
2. set `inDevelopment: true`
3. Make the sandbox work on your branch locally as well as on CI
4. Run `generate-sandboxes` GitHub action (just guessing the name here) to make sure the sandbox is published to `storybookjs/sandboxes`
5. Remove the `inDevelopment: true` flag and as soon as CI passes, merge the PR.

If you look at the graph on CircleCI, you'll see a group of jobs under a hub called `code`.

I interesting detail is that the graph is alphabetically sorted.

I wanted to present the most information at a glance in the CircleCI graph, so the jobs like `lint`, `typecheck` etc, should be near each other at the top; hence I grouped them in a hub.

I named the hub `code` because, well I needed something that was higher in the alphabet and `code` was descriptive enough; it hints at jobs related to the `./code` directory in our monorepo.

I debated the naming a bit with @ghengeveld last week; but I do not have a personal preference, I'll rename the file and hub to `common-jobs`, as you suggest.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Fragile array indexing: Replace hardcoded indices with named references.**

Lines 347 and 364 access `sandbox.jobs[1]` assuming it's the build job. If the job order in `defineSandboxFlow` changes (lines 318-337), this will break silently.



<details>
<summary>🔧 Suggested refactor for maintainability</summary>

Consider restructuring `defineSandboxFlow` to return a named object:

```typescript
// In defineSandboxFlow, instead of returning:
return {
  name: key,
  path,
  jobs,
};

// Return:
return {
  name: key,
  path,
  jobs: {
    create: createJob,
    build: buildJob,
    dev: devJob,
    chromatic: chromaticJob,
    vitest: vitestJob,
    e2e: e2eJob,
    testRunner: testRunnerJob,
  },
  allJobs: jobs, // flat array for backward compatibility
};

// Then in defineSandboxTestRunner:
[sandbox.jobs.build] // instead of sandbox.jobs[1]
```

This makes dependencies explicit and prevents silent breakage.
</details>
